scope: Cashier UI opening-float and refund EGP-to-piastres conversion only
assessment: Confirmed a reachable scale/rounding mismatch on these two cashier UI paths. Both accept any current-culture decimal and convert EGP*100 using Math.Round default ToEven; neither rejects more than two decimal places nor applies the max representable-piastres bound used by CashInput.TryParse. Money.FromEgp uses AwayFromZero. For a user-entered exact half-piastre amount such as 10.005 EGP, the UI path rounds 1000.5 piastres to 1000 (ToEven), whereas the Money boundary policy rounds to 1001 (AwayFromZero); opening float or refund can differ by one piastre. This is source-supported for reachable text-box paths, not runtime reproduced. Server receives integer piastres, so it cannot recover the entered precision or chosen rounding intent. Server protections bound consequence: Shift.Open rejects negative opening balances and positive floats are subject to active-day, account balance and transaction controls; RefundOrderHandler floors negative requests to zero, rejects zero, caps the requested integer to refundable remainder and checks source-account balance. These do not restore the user's unambiguous precision contract, but prevent this conversion mismatch from producing a refund above remaining amount or spending above protected balance. Excessively large decimal text may overflow at the client cast before a request, a UI error/availability concern rather than posted money. Main disposition: minor input correctness risk; unify cashier parsing with a shared bounded two-decimal parser (or explicitly define rounding), and add tests for third decimal exact-midpoint, excess precision, negative, and maximum amount. Static only.

source_references.claim: Reachable opening-float text parses current-culture decimal, allows any scale, multiplies and rounds with default midpoint behavior.
Reachable refund text parses current-culture decimal, allows any scale, rounds to integer piastres; UI later shows whole-piastre result.
Both inputs are ordinary text boxes with no visible precision/bound validation.
Existing helper explicitly bounds piastres and rejects more than two decimals, but specified Cashier paths do not call it.
Money.FromEgp uses AwayFromZero midpoint rounding, unlike current UI conversion.
Server accepts integer piastres; Shift.Open and positive-float account/day checks bound negative or overspend behavior.
Shift.Open rejects a negative opening float.
Refund handler clamps to remaining, rejects nonpositive safe amount and checks protected account balance.

execution: Read-only source review. No input automation, API call, database transaction or test execution.
example: 10.005 EGP -> 1000.5 piastres; Math.Round default ToEven => 1000. Money.FromEgp => AwayFromZero => 1001.
limitations: Only the listed cashier client view models and handlers were inspected. No evidence establishes the actual user entry distribution or whether third-decimal input is expected to be allowed. No database writes or live verification.
